# dualplot

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ryo-asashi/dualplot/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ryo-asashi/dualplot/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**dualplot** provides a unified, lightweight set of 2D plotting primitives that render seamlessly with either **Base R graphics** (`engine = "graphics"`) or **ggplot2** (`engine = "ggplot2"`).

Designed as a zero-heavy-dependency visualization backend for statistical and machine learning packages (such as `midr`), **dualplot** keeps `ggplot2` strictly in `Suggests` while offering bidirectional aesthetic translation, unified legends, and clean monograph styling across both backends.

## Installation

You can install the development version of **dualplot** from [GitHub](https://github.com/ryo-asashi/dualplot) with:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ryo-asashi/dualplot")
```

## Core Primitives

All six plotting primitives share a consistent interface (`theme`, `theme.values`, `legend`, `legend.title`, `engine`, and `...`):

| Function | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `draw_bars()` | Horizontal/vertical bar charts, dot charts (`type = "dot"`), grouped bars, and waterfall charts (`connect = TRUE`) |
| `draw_lines()` | Multi-line series and ICE curves over continuous or discrete x-axes, with optional point overlays |
| `draw_points()` | Scatter and jitter plots with continuous or discrete color mapping and Base overlay support |
| `draw_boxes()` | Horizontal or vertical grouped boxplots |
| `draw_matrix()` | Symmetric or square matrix heatmaps (e.g., correlation or pairwise interaction importance matrices) |
| `draw_surface()` | 2D grid heatmaps / interaction surfaces with optional data-point overlays |

## Quick Example

```{r example}
library(dualplot)

effects <- c(Age = 0.42, Income = -0.60, Tenure = 0.68, Region = -0.36)
cm <- cor(mtcars[, 1:5])

# 1. Base R graphics (zero ggplot2 dependency)
old_par <- par_monograph(mfrow = c(1, 2))
draw_bars(
  effects,
  theme = "Zissou 1",
  xlab = "Contribution",
  legend = "right",
  legend.title = "Effect",
  engine = "graphics"
)
draw_matrix(
  cm,
  theme = "Cividis",
  xlab = "Correlation",
  legend = "right",
  legend.title = "Corr",
  engine = "graphics"
)
par(old_par)
```

```{r example-gg}
# 2. Switch seamlessly to ggplot2
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
p1 <- draw_bars(
  effects,
  theme = "Zissou 1",
  xlab = "Contribution",
  legend = "right",
  legend.title = "Effect",
  engine = "ggplot2"
) +
  theme_monograph(grid.type = "x")
p2 <- draw_matrix(
  cm,
  theme = "Cividis",
  xlab = "Correlation",
  legend = "right",
  legend.title = "Corr",
  engine = "ggplot2"
) +
  theme_monograph()
p1 + p2
```

## Global Options & Styling

* **Engine selection**: Set the default rendering backend globally via `dualplot_options(engine = "ggplot2")` or `dualplot_options(engine = "graphics")`.
* **Default ggplot2 theme**: Attach a default theme automatically to all `ggplot2` outputs via `dualplot_options(gg.theme = theme_monograph())`.
* **Unified parameter translation**: Pass either Base R (`col`, `pch`, `cex`, `lty`, `lwd`, `main`) or `ggplot2` (`colour`, `shape`, `size`, `linetype`, `linewidth`, `title`) aesthetic arguments to any `draw_*()` function; **dualplot** translates and filters them automatically for the active backend.
* **Unified legends**: Control legend visibility and placement across both engines using `legend = TRUE` / `FALSE`, inside corners (`"topright"`, `"topleft"`, `"bottomright"`, `"bottomleft"`), or outside margins (`"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, `"right"`).
